solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some of the finest fur coats displayed around here?

definitions.text: Some of the finest fur coats displayed around here?

indicators.note: turned around, the run of letters is read from right to left
only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run sitting inside them

parts.note: the run straddling the end of finest, all of fur and the start of coats

explanation.surface: Pedigree animals with the most luxurious coats are on parade at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Semi-&lit: the whole clue describes the place, while its middle supplies the letters. CRUFTS is Britain's famous annual dog show.
explanation.definitionFit: At the dog show the best-groomed pedigree pets parade their coats before judges, so this is where fine fur is exhibited.

clue.text: Eggs to include acceptable one and one green

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so the eggs wrap round what follows

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
OK means acceptable, and I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: put eggs in, along with one green item.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says one twice: the first is wordplay, the second belongs to the definition, a green person being a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a novice, someone inexperienced or green, so one green person is a newcomer.

clue.text: See 14
Memorable phrase in confined area attributed to Spooner?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of pairs of words

parts.note: bound means confined and a site is an area; swap their first sounds

explanation.surface: A quotable line about a cramped place, credited to the Oxford don famous for verbal slips.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound bite is a short catchy quotation, the kind of memorable phrase replayed in news broadcasts.

clue.text: Quarrel somewhat drunkenly among the gods? That's Carol!

parts.note: a ding-dong is British slang for a heated row
merry is British for slightly drunk, tipsy
the gods live up above, in the heavens

explanation.surface: A tipsy squabble on Olympus, then the exclamation that it is all really a festive song.
explanation.walkthrough: A ding-dong is a noisy argument in British usage, and merry means mildly drunk. The pieces simply line up in order.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known Christmas carol with a Gloria refrain, sung each December.

clue.text: US airport over time becomes most dreary

parts.note: Dulles is the international airport serving Washington DC
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Waiting for ages at an American airport makes it the dullest place imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the airport sits on top of T.
explanation.definitionFit: Dullest is the superlative of dull, meaning the most boring or dreary.

clue.text: Going in starkers is grand way to attract attention

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, which encloses it

parts.note: starkers is British slang for naked
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Streaking past people is a sure-fire way to get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Starkers is British slang for stark naked; G goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle push with the elbow, a quiet way to catch someone's attention.

clue.text: Very easy task bringing in river debris

indicators.note: bringing something in means taking it inside, so the task wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a doss is British slang for a task needing no effort
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An undemanding job clearing rubbish out of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Doss in British slang is something done with no effort at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is waste matter or rubbish, worthless debris left over.

clue.text: Write article to support nearly-new drink that relieves sorrow

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
to pen is to write
the definite article

explanation.surface: Instructions to write an article endorsing a new drink that cures sadness.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece supporting another means it sits underneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, nepenthe is a potion that banishes grief, a drug of forgetfulness.

clue.text: Quintessential Englishman can talk nonsense

parts.note: both can and john are slang for a toilet
bull is slang for nonsense talk

explanation.surface: The archetypal Englishman is capable of spouting rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is not the verb of ability but the noun, slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bull is the stout cartoon figure personifying England, as Uncle Sam does America.

clue.text: Back yard fencing weak and sagging

indicators.note: going back means the whole result is read in the opposite direction
a fence goes round something, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: yd is the abbreviation for yard
poor means feeble or weak

explanation.surface: A garden fence at the rear of the property is flimsy and leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something droopy hangs down limply, the same as sagging.

clue.text: Licentious criminal Blair indicted at last

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of indicted

explanation.surface: A tabloid line about a former prime minister finally charged and accused of debauchery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribald means coarsely humorous and vulgar, near in sense to licentious or lewd.

clue.text: Still good to receive Novak's first service

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it inside, so the outer pieces enclose it

parts.note: even so means still, nevertheless

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the name before it

parts.note: the opening letter of Novak
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Djokovic's serve is still good: a tennis commentator's line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like Novak Djokovic's tennis serve, but it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, sung in cathedrals.

clue.text: Where Neagh is, lough showing duck?

parts.note: Lough Neagh lies in Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
L is short for lake or lough

explanation.surface: Asking which Northern Irish lake has a duck swimming on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero; Lough Neagh is the biggest lake in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman out without scoring makes a duck, which is a score of nothing.

clue.text: Dance article, not serious, sensational with spin applied

indicators.note: applied means put on, so this piece is attached ahead of the rest

parts.note: a trip is a short journey, a spin
the definite article
light means not serious, as in light reading
fantastic means sensational

explanation.surface: A feature article about dance, frivolous and thrilling, with a twist added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' suggests twirling in dance, but here it means a short trip, as in a spin in the car.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip the light fantastic is a jocular idiom, from Milton, meaning to dance.

clue.text: With online scam over, tightwad endlessly cut spending

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is removed

parts.note: an electronic con, a fraud carried out online
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a tightwad is a stingy person

explanation.surface: With an internet fraud done with, the stingy person still trims expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to save money by reducing expenditure.

clue.text: Canine say barking no matter what

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy and rearrange

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog's voice is its bark, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' fits the dog, but it is short for 'barking mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: In any case means regardless, whatever the circumstances.

clue.text: Check having to board earlier vessel

indicators.note: boarding means getting on and inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: sooner means earlier
ch is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A ticket inspection before getting on a boat that left ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship, and also a large beer glass; both are vessels.

clue.text: Float in E Med and Corsica, stormy area

indicators.note: stormy waters churn things up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the eastern Mediterranean, taken as written
the island taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Drifting in the eastern Mediterranean and off Corsica, a rough patch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Float' seems to be about bobbing in the sea, but it is a noun: a soda drink with ice cream floating in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A float is a fizzy drink topped with a scoop of ice cream, an ice-cream soda.

clue.text: Carried by British sailors, American took flight

indicators.note: something carried is held inside the carrier, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Royal Navy
A is short for American

explanation.surface: An American borne along by Royal Navy crew managed to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran here means fled; to take flight is to run away.

clue.text: See 5 across
Dry quarters needed in Pacific

parts.note: sere means dried up, withered
two compass points, North and East, the quarters

explanation.surface: Arid living quarters are required on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' looks like the ocean, but it is the adjective meaning peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific in lower case means peaceful and calm, which is what serene means.

clue.text: Muse to incarcerate old woman in scented container

indicators.note: to incarcerate is to lock up inside, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to muse is to ponder
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: A poet's muse locks an elderly lady up in a perfumed box.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomander is a ball or case filled with fragrant spices, carried or hung to scent the air.

clue.text: Inclined to be an idiot having assimilated Pound

indicators.note: assimilating something absorbs it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tit is British slang for a fool
L, from libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone prone to foolishness after absorbing the poet Ezra Pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Tit is British slang for a twit; the L goes before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Atilt means tilted, leaning at an angle, so inclined in the physical sense.

clue.text: Westminster in cover up getting third degree?

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
in means placed inside, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: a lid is a cover
the Houses of Parliament at Westminster, abbreviated HP

explanation.surface: A Westminster cover-up leading to a harsh interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third degree' looks like police grilling; a doctorate is the third university degree, after bachelor's and master's. DPhil is Oxford's name for a PhD.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate follows a bachelor's and a master's, making it the third academic qualification.

clue.text: Plato finally co-ordinates knowledge — it's inspired

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the name before it

parts.note: the closing letter of Plato
x and y are the axes of graph co-ordinates
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Plato's ideas finally arranged into wisdom: a philosophy of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired' means breathed in, not creatively brilliant. Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxygen is the gas taken into the lungs, so it is what is breathed in.

clue.text: See 5 across
One couple going without sex: daughter followed suit

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: going outside something means wrapping round it

parts.note: to couple is to mate
it is slang for sex appeal or sex
D is short for daughter

explanation.surface: A celibate pair, and their daughter did the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here is the old sense of outside, not lacking; the surface wants it to mean abstaining.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow suit is to copy what someone else did, which is to imitate.

clue.text: Save friend Romeo stabs, showing cruel aspect

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, matching the adverb answer

indicators.note: a stab goes into something, so one letter is driven inside the other piece

parts.note: save and but both mean except
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A plea to rescue a friend whom Romeo stabs, a cruel scene from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' is not rescue but the preposition meaning except. Romeo did stab Mercutio's killer Tybalt.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting brutally means acting savagely, displaying a cruel side.

clue.text: On level terms with the Spanish team

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
even means level, neither side ahead

explanation.surface: A sports report: the scores are level against the Spanish side.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish article comes first, though the clue gives it second.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has eleven players, so the number names the team.
